To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
direct-to-PCR tissue sampling and preservation can be achieved by using either a custom preparation or one of two commercially available preservatives.
direct-to-PCR DNA profiling of human tissue samples can be performed successfully using a variety of preservatives.
DNA profiles can be obtained without DNA extraction, from fresh or decomposed tissue, preserved in a variety of solutions, and stored at −80°C for 4+ years, without loss of DNA profile information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a direct-to-PCR method of tissue preservation for DVI and forensic DNA profiling.
a simple and rapid DNA preservation method that allows DNA profiling without DNA extraction.
developing a simple, robust and cost-effective method for DNA profiling in DVI and similar situations where refrigeration is not available.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of any of these preservatives in conjunction with direct-to-PCR DNA profiling would be an effective means of preserving DNA for DVI purposes.
the use of any of the preservatives described herein would be a useful addition to the DVI process.
the addition of preservative solutions to fresh or decomposing human tissue samples can provide sufficient template DNA for PCR amplification and DNA profiling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

direct-to-PCR tissue storage is a reliable method of preserving DNA for subsequent DNA profiling, and that the DNA profiles obtained are as good as those produced by DNA extracted from the tissue samples.
direct-to-PCR DNA typing is a robust and reliable method for obtaining DNA profiles from human tissue preserved in a variety of solutions, including those containing DMSO.
the use of DMSO and TENT buffer, DNAgard and the Tissue Stabilizing Kit as direct-to-PCR preservatives is a promising approach to DNA profiling of human tissue samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that

direct-to-PCR DNA profiling from tissue preserved in a variety of preservatives is possible, and this method could be used in DVI to increase the probability of DNA typing and decrease the time required for DNA profiling.
DNA profiling can be performed directly from preservative solutions surrounding human muscle tissue, without the need for tissue extraction or DNA purification.
DNA profiling of human tissue can be achieved by direct-to-PCR DNA sampling and preservation.
